title: Longest Ideal Subsequence
summary: Given a string s of lowercase letters and an integer k, find the longest subsequence t of s where the absolute difference in alphabet order between any two adjacent letters in t is at most k.
statement: Given a string s of lowercase letters and an integer k, find the longest subsequence t of s where the absolute difference in alphabet order between any two adjacent letters in t is at most k. Return the length of this longest ideal subsequence.
constraints: Choose a subsequence without changing character order.
Adjacent chosen letters may differ by at most k in alphabet position.
Return the maximum possible subsequence length.
hints: Store the best ideal-subsequence length ending at each of the 26 letters.
For the current letter x, inspect prior ending letters in the inclusive range x-k through x+k.
Extend the best compatible subsequence by one and update the slot for x.
Every valid predecessor is in that range, and retaining only the best length per ending letter is sufficient for all future extensions.
editorial: Every valid predecessor is in that range, and retaining only the best length per ending letter is sufficient for all future extensions.

tests.explanation: One longest valid subsequence is a,c,b,d; every adjacent alphabet difference is at most two, so the length is four.
With zero allowed difference, only identical adjacent chosen letters are valid; each letter occurs once, so the answer is one.
